text:
Bobby McMann scored 29 goals last season, split between Toronto and Seattle, and this fall the goals have mostly dried up. He has three in 19 games and none in his last ten, with two points over that stretch against about five we'd expect at his ice time.

The shots are still coming. He has 48 on goal, and his own expected goals (the quality of his chances) sit at 0.90 per 60 minutes, right where they were last season. What's missing is the finish: he is shooting 6.2%, below the bottom of our talent range for him (11.2% to 15.6%). That part usually turns.

The bigger worry is the rest of his game. At five on five the Kraken get only 42.1% of the expected goals with him on, 4.3 points worse than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has 53% of his shots coming off the rush, and his top speed is in the 95th percentile, so watch whether Seattle can get him the puck in open ice again. Evolving-Hockey noted he faced the other team's best last season.
headline: Bobby McMann is shooting, but nothing is going in
